newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian is youngest to sail non-stop round world.
newsitem.headline: Australian is youngest to sail non-stop round world.

text.p: An Australian teenager received a hero's welcome on Sunday after becoming the youngest person ever to sail around the world solo and non-stop.

But 18-year-old David Dicks and his 10-metre sloop Seaflight had to be towed into this Western Australian port because of adverse winds and obstruction from a 300-strong fleet of other boats gathered to greet him.

Sailing club officials said Dicks passed the real finishing line 11 kms (seven miles) out to sea late on Friday, when he crossed the opposite geographical bearing to the one he turned on off Bermuda in July.
He had hoped to make the extra distance unaided but had to be towed until the last 800 metres because of a headwind.
Hundreds of other vessels, including yachts, ferries, surfskis and even an old pearling lugger, made matters worse by stirring up the sea and effectively becalming the boy sailor.
Some 15,000 people crowded the wharfs to witness Fremantle's greatest sailing moment since Western Australian entrepreneur Alan Bond -- now in jail for fraud -- brought back the Americas Cup in 1983.
Dicks, from the nearby city of Perth, has covered more than 50,000 kms (30,000 miles) since leaving Fremantle on February 26. He turned 18 last month.
During his 264 days at sea, Dicks also became the youngest person to sail around Cape Horn -- a feat made all the more impressive because he did it in winter with a damaged sail.
Welcoming the teenager home, Western Australian state premier Richard Court told him: "I still can't comprehend how you have endured the hardship of the last nine months."
Dicks had been hoping to become the youngest person to sail around the world unassisted. But he was forced to borrow a bolt from the British navy to repair his mast off the Falkland Islands in May.
The previous record for the youngest sailor to circumnavigate the globe single-handed was held by American Robert Lee Graham, who sailed from the U.S. West Coast aged 16 in 1965.
But Graham took five years to complete the trip after stopping off to get married on the way.
